prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name one single “best” attorney — the best lawyer for you depends on the facts of your case, the seriousness of your injuries, your goals (quick settlement vs. trial), and your comfort with the lawyer. That said, Chicago has several well‑known, highly regarded personal injury firms that frequently handle car-accident cases. Below I’ll give practical guidance, a short list of reputable firms to consider, and next steps.

Reputable Chicago firms often recommended for car-accident claims
- Clifford Law Offices — well known for high‑profile crash and wrongful‑death cases and trial experience.  
- Corboy & Demetrio — long history in catastrophic injury and wrongful‑death litigation in Chicago.  
- Levin & Perconti — focuses on catastrophic injuries and has a strong track record in major verdicts and settlements.  
- Romanucci & Blandin — experienced with auto collisions, wrongful death and serious injury cases.  
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard — regular plaintiffs’ practice handling auto crashes and traumatic injuries.  
- Power Rogers & Smith — established Chicago personal-injury firm that handles auto accidents and insurance disputes.

How to choose the right lawyer for your case
- Look for specific experience with car-accident claims and with injuries like yours (neck/back, TBI, spinal injury, wrongful death).  
- Trial experience and resources: lawyers who will take cases to trial usually get better offers from insurers.  
- Track record: settlements/verdicts and client references.  
- Communication: responsiveness and clear explanations.  
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (commonly ~33% — confirm exact terms and costs).  
- Discipline check: verify there are no ethics complaints via the Illinois Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission (ARDC).  
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Chicago courts, hospitals, and expert witnesses is helpful.

Where to research and verify lawyers
- Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, Avvo/Justia/Bloomberg Law profiles, and Best Lawyers.  
- Illinois State Bar and ARDC to check standing and any disciplinary history.  
- Google/ Yelp client reviews and firm news (verdicts/settlements).

Questions to ask at a free consult
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the outcomes?  
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day? Will you go to trial if needed?  
- What are your fees and who pays litigation costs?  
- What is your strategy and estimate of value? How long will it take?  
- Can you provide references from recent clients?

Documents to bring to a consultation
- Police report, photos of the scene/vehicles/injuries, medical records and bills, insurance information, correspondence with insurers, wage-loss documentation, and any witness contact info.

Timing: act fast
- Illinois generally has a 2‑year statute of limitations for personal injury claims (exceptions apply). Don’t delay contacting a lawyer.

If you want, tell me:
- a zip code or neighborhood, the date/severity of the crash, and the main question (maximize recovery, need trial attorney, low‑value claim, uninsured motorist, etc.), and I’ll look up 3–5 attorneys or local firms that match your needs and provide contact links and recent accomplishments.
